content:
- Model tends to overestimate prices in the short term (especially after recent spikes) and underestimates during sustained downward sentiment.  
- Overshoots occur after positive sentiment spikes; model reacts too aggressively, then corrects too late.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., >3 consecutive negative values), model underestimates and fails to anticipate further decline.  
- When sentiment is mixed or trending upward, model often overcorrects downward, missing the upward momentum.  
- Model exhibits lag in responding to sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment turns negative mid-period, forecast still holds high values.  
- Mean reversion is overemphasized — model assumes prices will return to historical mean too quickly, ignoring sentiment-driven volatility.  
- For 30-day horizon, model is overly sensitive to recent 1-2 day sentiment extremes, leading to erratic corrections.  
- When sentiment is high and price is rising, model often underestimates the continuation of the trend.  
- Model tends to underestimate the depth of corrections during strong negative sentiment, especially if preceded by a spike.
